name: Acenocoumarol
executiveSummary: Vitamin K antagonist (more used than warfarin in LatAm/Europe). Adult: typical start **2–4 mg PO/day** (elderly **1 mg**); adjust to INR (e.g. **2–3**). Shorter half-life than warfarin — faster swings. Antidote: vitamin K ± PCC.
indications:
## Indications

- AF, DVT/PE, mechanical valves, other VKA indications per local guideline.

## Precautions

- Same interactions/bleeding as warfarin; frequent INR at start.
- Pregnancy: teratogenic — alternatives.
- Do not self-adjust; same daily time.

> Institutional nomograms (do not copy warfarin tables 1:1).

adulto.dose: Usual start **2–4 mg/day** × 1–2 days (frail **1 mg**), then by INR. Typical maintenance **1–8 mg/day**. Bridge with heparin until therapeutic INR if needed.
adulto.notes: Counsel on vitamin K diet and INR-altering drugs.

pediatrico.dose: Hematology only — no standard ambulatory regimen.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Bleeding, bruising; rare skin necrosis; teratogenicity.
